patients.summary: Administrative assistant who joined the practice at 27 weeks of her second pregnancy with a history of gestational hypertension. Severe preeclampsia with AKI and hypertensive retinopathy at 35 weeks in October 2024, then eclampsia at 34 weeks in her third pregnancy in October 2025; both resolved postpartum on short courses of nifedipine.

documents.body: Caller wants to set up primary care here. Has had no PCP since her old practice closed its panel to her plan. Currently about 25 weeks pregnant, OB care with an outside OB group and she plans to keep them for the pregnancy. Membership paperwork emailed. New patient visit booked 8/20 at 8:40. Asked her to have her prior practice and OB send records.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, establishing primary care.

Emily is 32, G2P1, currently 27w1d by an LMP of 2/12/24. Prenatal care is with an outside OB group and going smoothly so far by her account. She wanted a primary care home for after the baby and for her own long-term health. No complaints today. No headaches, no visual changes, no swelling beyond the end of the day.

OB history: first pregnancy 2021, term vaginal delivery. Developed gestational hypertension late in that pregnancy, no meds needed after delivery and pressures came back to normal postpartum. Because of that history her OB started her on aspirin 81 mg at 12 weeks this time. Also on a prenatal vitamin.

PMH: as above, otherwise none. PSH: none.
Meds: prenatal vitamin with folic acid 1 tab daily; aspirin 81 mg daily (OB).
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother had preeclampsia with her pregnancies. Father has hypertension. Otherwise noncontributory.
SH: married, works as an administrative assistant. Never smoked, does not drink.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP normal. Pleasant, well appearing, gravid. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen gravid, fundus consistent with dates, nontender. Trace ankle edema only. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Skin without rash.

Assessment/plan:
1. Pregnancy, 27 weeks, with history of gestational hypertension and a mother with preeclampsia. Higher risk for a hypertensive disorder this time. Agree with aspirin. Reviewed warning signs: severe headache, vision change, RUQ or upper belly pain, sudden swelling, shortness of breath. These go to L&D or the ED, not a call-back. OB is following BP at every visit.
2. Baseline labs today: CMP and CBC so we have her own numbers on file.
3. Health maintenance: will request prior-practice records for Pap history. Flu shot this fall, can do it here.

RTC after delivery, sooner prn.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Emily, your labs from yesterday look good. Kidney function is normal (creatinine 0.7), liver tests normal, and your hemoglobin is 11.6, which is a typical number for this point in pregnancy. Nothing to do. Nice to meet you.

documents.title: Prenatal Records, Outside OB Group
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Prenatal record summary, received by fax.

Patient: Emily Lemieux, DOB 04/22/1992. G2P1001. LMP 02/12/2024, EDD 11/18/2024, dating confirmed by first-trimester ultrasound.

History: gestational hypertension in prior pregnancy (2021), resolved after delivery. Family history of preeclampsia (mother).
Medications: prenatal vitamin daily. Low-dose aspirin 81 mg daily started at 12 weeks for preeclampsia risk reduction, continue to 36 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.

Prenatal labs: antibody screen negative. Rubella immune. HBsAg negative. HIV negative. Hepatitis C antibody negative. RPR nonreactive. Urine culture negative. First-trimester screen low risk. Anatomy survey at 20 weeks normal. Glucose challenge at 26 weeks normal.

Blood pressures at all visits through 26 weeks in the normal range. Urine protein negative at each visit.

Plan: routine prenatal visits, Tdap at 28-32 weeks in office, BP at each visit.

Records from prior primary care practice, 2019-2023.

Problem list: history of gestational hypertension (2021).

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu vaccine. 32 weeks pregnant, OB aware and agrees. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid, VIS provided. BP normal today. Tolerated well, waited 15 min without issue.

events.reason: Severe headache and blurry vision, 35 weeks pregnant

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 10/18/2024. Copy received 10/23/2024.

CC: headache, blurry vision.

HPI: 32 y/o G2P1 at 35w4d by early ultrasound. Woke yesterday with a headache that has been severe all day and night, not relieved by rest, and her vision has been blurry since yesterday afternoon. Pregnancy uncomplicated to this point per patient and OB record. Prior pregnancy with gestational hypertension. Denies seizure, chest pain, shortness of breath. Fetal movement present.

Meds: prenatal vitamin daily; aspirin 81 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with preeclampsia; father with chronic hypertension.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, works as an administrative assistant.

Vitals: BP 155/100 on arrival and 155/100 again on repeat 15 minutes later. HR 90s, afebrile, SpO2 98% RA.
Exam: uncomfortable but alert and oriented. Fundoscopy with arteriolar narrowing and cotton wool spots. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Gravid, nontender. 2+ edema of both lower legs. DTRs 3+, no clonus. No focal neuro deficit.

Labs: Hgb 11.0 g/dL. Platelets 95,000/uL. Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL (baseline 0.7 on prenatal labs). AST 70 U/L, ALT 80 U/L. UA protein 2+.
Fetal heart tones in the 140s, reactive tracing on L&D monitor.

ED course: IV labetalol given with improvement in pressure. Magnesium sulfate load and infusion started for seizure prophylaxis. OB at bedside.

Impression: severe preeclampsia without HELLP features. Acute kidney injury. Hypertensive retinopathy.
Disposition: admitted to labor and delivery under OB for delivery planning.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery. Admitted 10/18/2024, discharged 10/22/2024. Received 10/23/2024.

Admitting diagnosis: severe preeclampsia without HELLP features at 35w4d, with acute kidney injury and hypertensive retinopathy.

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED on magnesium sulfate after IV labetalol. Pressures controlled with as-needed IV labetalol. Cervix favorable; induction with oxytocin. Uncomplicated vaginal delivery early on 10/19/2024 of a liveborn infant. Blood loss within normal limits. Magnesium continued 24 hours postpartum, no seizure activity. Headache and visual blurring resolved by postpartum day 1. Pressures settled into the 130s-140s/80s-90s; started nifedipine ER 30 mg daily on postpartum day 1.

Discharge labs 10/22: creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, platelets 162,000/uL, AST 38 U/L, ALT 44 U/L.

Discharge medications: nifedipine ER 30 mg daily. Prenatal vitamin daily. Aspirin discontinued.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: BP check with PCP within one week. Home BP twice daily, call for 160/110 or higher, severe headache or vision change. Postpartum visit with OB in 6 weeks. Eye follow-up recommended for the retinal findings.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt day after discharge, records in from hospital this AM. She and baby home, doing well. Taking nifedipine 30 daily, has a home cuff, readings 128-140/84-90. No headache, vision back to normal, no RUQ pain, swelling going down. Off aspirin per OB. Reviewed when to call/go to ED. Visit with PCP Friday 10/25 confirmed.

orders.reason: Hypertensive retinopathy with cotton wool spots during severe preeclampsia

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u, 6 days postpartum.

S: Seen in the ED 10/18 at 35w4d with severe headache and blurry vision, BP 155/100, platelets 95K, Cr 1.2 (her baseline here was 0.7 in August), AST/ALT 70/80, 2+ proteinuria, cotton wool spots on fundoscopy. Dx severe preeclampsia. Mag, labetalol, induced, SVD 10/19. Discharge Cr 0.9, plt 162. Went home on nifedipine ER 30.
Feels fine. Tired, baby feeding every 2-3 h. Headache gone, vision normal. No RUQ pain, no SOB. Home BPs 126-140/82-90. Off aspirin.

Meds: nifedipine ER 30 mg daily, prenatal vitamin.

O: BP 138/88 here. Well appearing. Fundi not dilated, no papilledema on undilated look. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, fundus firm below umbilicus. Trace edema at ankles. Reflexes 2+, no clonus. PHQ-9 = 3.

A/P:
1. Postpartum hypertension after severe preeclampsia: acceptable on nifedipine ER 30. Keep home log, send readings next week. Call for 150/100 or above, or any headache or vision change.
2. AKI: rechecking CMP today.
3. Hypertensive retinopathy: referral to ophthalmology for dilated exam in 4-6 weeks.
4. Prenatal vitamin can continue.
5. Mood screen reassuring, has support at home.

RTC 6 weeks postpartum (early Dec), sooner prn.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Emily, good news. Kidney number is down to 0.8, almost back to your August value. Platelets and liver tests are back to normal. Keep the nifedipine going and keep sending your home readings.

documents.title: Home BP Readings
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, here's my week. Mornings mostly 122/80 to 128/84, evenings a little higher, highest was 132/86 Tuesday. No headaches. Is that ok? Should I keep checking twice a day?

documents.title: RE: Home BP Readings
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Those look very good. Stay on the nifedipine for now and keep checking once a day is fine. We'll talk about stopping it at your visit in December.

documents.body: Pharmacy fax: refill request nifedipine ER 30 mg, hospital rx was 14 days. Pended 30 day supply, no refills, for PCP.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
6 wk postpartum f/u for BP.

Doing well. Home BPs the last 2 weeks 108-120/68-78 on nifedipine ER 30, a couple of lightheaded moments standing up fast. No headaches, vision fine. Saw OB last week for her postpartum visit, all ok there.

BP 116/74, rest of vitals as charted. Looks well. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema. PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. Postpartum HTN resolved. Stop nifedipine today. Check home BP a few times a week for 2 weeks, then weekly for a month; send me numbers if over 135/85.
2. Severe preeclampsia, now resolved. AKI resolved if today's Cr is back to baseline, rechecking BMP/CBC/LFT. Putting history of preeclampsia on the problem list.
3. Talked about what this means long-term: having preeclampsia raises lifetime risk of high blood pressure and heart disease, so yearly BP, lipids and sugar from here on. For any future pregnancy: early OB visit, aspirin from 12 weeks, baseline labs, and let us know as soon as she's pregnant.
4. Eye appt with ophthalmology 12/10.
5. COVID booster today. Flu done in Sept.

RTC for a physical in about a year.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Emily, creatinine is 0.7, right back to your baseline. Blood counts and liver tests normal. The kidney injury from October has fully recovered.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Thank you for sending Ms. Lemieux, 32, seen 12/10/2024 for follow-up of retinal changes noted during severe preeclampsia in October (arteriolar narrowing and cotton wool spots per the hospital record).

She reports clear vision since delivery. No floaters, flashes or field loss. Allergies: NKDA. Meds: none besides a prenatal vitamin; postpartum nifedipine stopped last week.

VA 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. Pupils equal, no APD. IOP 14/15. Anterior segment quiet OU.
Dilated fundus exam: discs pink and sharp, C/D 0.3 OU. Vessels of normal caliber, no AV nicking. No cotton wool spots, hemorrhages or exudates. Macula flat with good foveal reflex OU. Periphery attached.

Impression: hypertensive retinopathy of pregnancy, resolved. Normal fundus exam today.
Plan: no ophthalmic follow-up needed beyond routine eye care. Would re-examine if hypertension recurs.
